subnets.name: Compute Horde
subnets.description: computehorde is a specialized subnet (subnet 12) within the Bittensor network, designed to provide scalable, decentralized, and trusted GPU computing power for validators across other Bittensor subnets. By transforming untrusted GPUs from miners into reliable compute resources, computehorde reduces dependency on centralized services and enables cost-effective, large-scale validation. Key features include fair and verified work mechanisms, scalable mining with multiple executors per miner, hardware class-based resource allocation, a developer SDK for easy integration, collateral-based trust for organic jobs, and an optional DDoS shield for miners. The project aims to support a wide range of GPU types and offers a robust scoring and incentive system to ensure quality and accountability.

Validators evaluate these adapters for reasoning quality, efficiency, and compactness, rewarding those that improve performance without increasing resource demands. The system emphasizes repeatable evaluation, strict answer formatting, and fairness through deterministic shuffling and scoring. Submissions mature on-chain before evaluation, and the protocol supports integration with tools like Weights & Biases for live tracking. The project is tailored for efficient, scalable reasoning model improvements within a collaborative, on-chain environment.

subnets.name: ReadyAI
subnets.description: readyai is an open-source project that provides a low-cost, resource-efficient data structuring and semantic tagging pipeline for individuals and businesses. It transforms raw data into structured, AI-ready formats suitable for vector databases and AI applications. The system leverages distributed miners and validators, using large language models (LLMs) like OpenAI's GPT-4o to annotate and tag data. Validators establish ground truth and score miner submissions based on similarity metrics, ensuring data quality. The platform is designed for scalability, incentivizing data contribution and validation through a mining and rewards mechanism.

subnets.name: BitMind
subnets.description: Gas (Generative Adversarial Subnet) is a Bittensor subnet designed to advance AI-generated media detection and synthesis through open, incentivized competition. Inspired by generative adversarial networks (GANs), it features two parallel mining tracks: discriminative miners submit models to detect synthetic images, videos, and audio, while generative miners create synthetic media to challenge detectors. Validators orchestrate the process, scoring both miner types to ensure continuous improvement. The system uses weekly refreshed datasets, rewards novel and accurate models, and aims to keep detection tools evolving as rapidly as synthetic media threats.

subnets.description: dojo v2 is a decentralized generative adversarial network (GAN) platform built on Bittensor, designed to foster competitive AI model development through zero-sum incentives. Unlike traditional GANs, dojo v2 challenges miners to produce outputs that are not only indistinguishable from high-quality baselines but also superior, creating a dynamic environment where participants act as both generators and discriminators. Miners can easily participate without running servers by registering and using a browser wallet, while validators help maintain network integrity. The project emphasizes ease of entry, competitive AI advancement, and decentralized participation.

Babelbit targets critical industries and use cases where instant, natural multilingual communication is essential, positioning itself as a disruptive solution in the $100 billion language services market.

The platform aims to connect every AI model through a single, neutral hub, maximizing utility and minimizing gatekeeping.
